(oxiconazole) Profile Oxiconazole is an imidazole antifungal applied topically as the nitrate as a cream, solution, or powder equivalent to oxiconazole 1% in the treatment of fungal infections of the skin (p.521). It is also given as a pessary in a single dose equivalent to 600 mg of oxiconazole in the treatment of vaginal candidiasis (p.518). Local reactions including burning and itching have been report- ed. Intravaginal preparations of azoles may damage latex contra- ceptives. For a discussion of the caution needed when using azole antifun- gals during pregnancy, see under Pregnancy in Precautions of Fluconazole, p.532. ◊ Reviews. 1. Jegasothy BV, Pakes GE. Oxiconazole nitrate: pharmacology, ef- ficacy, and safety of a new imidazole antifungal agent. Clin Ther 1991; 13: 126–41.
